checks.a_analysis: Each content block from the source document appears only once in the elements array of the corresponding sections. Page-level headers (e.g., '2019 Governor’s NCWorks Awards of Distinction') that repeat on every page of the source are correctly normalized to appear only in the first section of the output, which follows standard accessibility practices for document conversion.

The heading hierarchy is flat and incorrect. All major headings, including the document title ('2019 Governor’s NCWorks Awards of Distinction'), award categories ('Wayne Daves Outstanding Achievement...'), and recipient names ('Amy Bryan', 'Jordan Shoffner') are assigned as level 3 headings (H3). This skips levels H1 and H2, providing no structural distinction between the document title, section categories, and subsections.
checks.b_evidence_source: The source defines a clear hierarchy: Document Title (Top), Award Category (Section Level), Recipient Name (Subsection Level).

checks.b_evidence_location: Throughout the document; headings-1 through heading-6 and others.

checks.a_analysis: The source document contains no tables, and no tables were generated in the output.

The reading flow is inconsistent regarding the award categories. On pages 1-5, the category headers (e.g., 'Outstanding Innovative Partnership', 'Outstanding Young Adult') are used as section titles but are missing from the elements array, meaning they are excluded from the primary reading flow of the document content. However, in Section 6, the category heading ('Wayne Daves Outstanding Achievement in Workforce Development') is included within the elements array. This inconsistency breaks the expected structural flow compared to the source document.
checks.b_evidence_source: Pages 1-5 contain visible headings for the award category (e.g., 'Outstanding Teen' on page 3).
checks.b_evidence_output: Section 3 (Outstanding Teen) starts its elements with Heading-4 ('Jordan Shoffner'), omitting the category label from the elements stream, whereas Section 6 includes the category label as the first element.

checks.a_analysis: The source document consists of narrative paragraphs and headings with no lists. The output correctly reflects this structure.
There are no links present in the source document, and none were injected into the output.

checks.a_analysis: The HTML document successfully translates the multi-page PDF layout into a single-column responsive flow. Decorative elements like the hexagonal patterns are appropriately hidden for accessibility. The visual organization follows the logical structure of the source, with awards grouped by category and followed by their respective narratives. The use of a full-page render for the first entry (Page 1) is an acceptable fallback for complex graphic layouts. While the layout is simplified compared to the PDF, information is presented in the correct sequence.
The source document does not contain any tables; it consists entirely of headers, narrative text, and images. Therefore, this check is not applicable.

Several meaningful images present in the source PDF are missing from the HTML output. While the first award (W.I.N. Specifically, the photos of Jordan Shoffner (page 3), Regina Durham (page 4), and Karen Rowe (page 7), as well as the TERO logo (page 5), do not appear in their respective sections in the HTML rendering, nor is there a fallback full-page image provided for those pages.
